events.label: Sam Vimes chases Carcer across rooftops in storm
events.description: Commander Sam Vimes, holding a murderer's collar in a lightning storm, chases the killer Carcer across the rooftops of Ankh-Morpork - and both are struck.

events.label: Magical storm flings both back to Glorious 25th of May past
events.description: The storm does something impossible: it throws Vimes and Carcer thirty years back into the city's past, to the week of the Revolution he remembers.

events.label: Arrive days before Treacle Mine Road uprising
events.description: Vimes lands days before the uprising on Treacle Mine Road - the same rebellion whose failure he grew up in the shadow of.

events.label: Meets young Sam Vimes — must mentor his own past
events.description: He meets the young, idealistic, hopeless constable he used to be - and realises he must teach his younger self how to be a policeman without ever saying who he is.

events.label: Vimes assumes identity of John Keel
events.description: With the real sergeant John Keel dead by Carcer's hand, Vimes takes the dead man's name - becoming, for one week, his own sergeant and teacher.

events.label: Carcer accelerates chaos; tries to remake history worse
events.description: Carcer aligns with the city's worst men and works to make the Revolution bloodier and the future darker - the history Vimes remembers is now only one possibility.

events.label: Trains young Sam and Night Watch into better men
events.description: Sergeant Keel - Vimes in disguise - drills the young Watch into something better: how to stand, how to look, how to be the line that holds.

events.label: Treacle Mine Road barricade; keeps history on rails
events.description: The barricades go up on Treacle Mine Road, and for a few shining days the little republic of the Watch holds its patch of the city honest.

events.label: History requires Keel's death — Vimes fulfills then escapes timing
events.description: History demands John Keel die in the fighting - and Vimes, playing Keel, walks into it knowing, then slips loose of the moment at the last breath.

events.label: Returns to present with Carcer for trial
events.description: The storm returns him to his own time with Carcer in tow - delivered, at last, to a trial the city can hold.

events.label: Lilac remembrance — Vimes was always his own mentor
events.description: Every year Vimes wears a sprig of lilac for the men of the Revolution - and now he knows why he always felt he owed them: he was there, he was one of them.

events.label: Present: birth of Young Sam (son) rhymes the loop
events.description: In the present, his son is born - young Sam, named for a father who is still, in a way that no one else can be, his own teacher.

events.label: Vimes thrown back to past Watch days
events.description: The storm that tore Vimes out of his own time and into the Watch's history.

events.label: Meets young Vetinari / young Vimes path
events.description: The young men of the past Watch - a young Vimes, a cool and dangerous young Vetinari - seen before they became themselves.

events.label: Must preserve Revolution history
events.description: The burden of the week: history must come out as remembered, or the city he loves will never exist.

events.label: Assumes John Keel identity
events.description: The stolen identity - Sergeant Keel, the man whose name Vimes will honour for the rest of his life.

events.label: Trains young Vimes
events.description: Teaching the young Watch what he learned the hard way - and learning it again by teaching it.

events.label: Becomes the mentor he remembered
events.description: The closed circle: the sergeant who made Vimes was Vimes, all along.

events.label: Returns to present altered slightly
events.description: A return to the present that is one good man's memory better than it was.

events.label: History has inertia; personal bootstrap
events.description: The rule of Discworld time: history is elastic but stubborn - it fights for its shape, and people are how it wins.

ruleEffects.effect: Keeping revolution 'on rails' fulfills the history Vimes remembers
Keel's teachings have no teacher but future Vimes

outcome.summary: Vimes was always Keel; Carcer returned for justice; lilac and newborn son close the rhyme.
